text:
Dr. Suzanne O'Brien
Psychiatrist
67 Sigmund Street
Brighton 3186
5/1/2009
Dear Dr. O'Brien,
Re: Ms Janet Bird
Thank you for seeing Ms Janet, a 16-year-old student whose features are suggestive of anorexia nervosa.
On 11/11/2007, she presented with a 3 month history of constipation. Her bowel action was once every 4 to5 days despite taking two tablespoons bran in the morning. Her examination was unremarkable apart from low weight which was 52 kg. She requested a strong laxative. However, I refused and advised her to increase vegetables, fluids and fibre in her diet.
Ms Janet's mother accompanied her on 28/12/2007 and she was warried regarding Janet's weight. On examination, she lost 5 kg of her weight in a month. Otherwise, no abnormalities were detected. Accordingly, thyroid function tests, liver function tests and full blood exam were requested.
On today's visit, I discovered that she had had false believe about her weight. She wanted her weight to be 40 kg. Moreover, she complained of over-reacting parents. Please note, her laboratory results were normal and she denied vomiting.
In view of the above, I would appreciate it if you provide an assessment of this patient as  well as advice regarding management and  treatment of her condition.
Should you have any queries, please do not hesitate to contact me.
Yours sincerely,
Doctor
